newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil lifts with stronger futures, premiums.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil lifts with stronger futures, premiums.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices burst into life on Thursday gaining up to $3 a tonne on the back of stronger futures and firmer premiums.
March IPE gas oil closed $2.75 a tonne stronger at $164.75, just 25 cents off the session high.
Premiums were assessed a touch stronger on the back of run cuts at some ARA refineries and an easing of supply, particuarly for Russian gas oil.
"I think we could see some demand coming in from refiners who have lost material because of run-cuts," said one gas oil trader.

BP and Texaco have both cut runs by about 12 percent at the 400,000 bpd Nerefco complex while throughput has fallen by 12-15 percent at Shell's 374,000 bpd Rotterdam refinery. Other refiners are thought to have also cut runs.

Barge premiums were about 50 cents stronger with a second half barge trading at March IPE +50 cents. But, demand was still fairly thin and some dealers said they had little confidence in today's price gains.
Russian premiums were steady around March IPE flat, but the tone was firming. Traders said it was becoming increasingly difficult to secure cargoes.
